title: Protected concerted activity, representation, and anti-surveillance boundary

observations.claim: Section 7 protects collective workplace action and prohibits employer interference, restraint or coercion.
limits: Private-sector statutory coverage and fact-specific protection remain open.

observations.claim: Protected concerted activity can include group complaints, petitions, safety concerns and contact with employers, agencies or media.
limits: Does not classify any named Wave 04 conduct as protected.

observations.claim: NLRB public case summaries include retaliation following safety reports, workplace complaints and collective communication, with remedies including backpay, reinstatement and record correction.
limits: Case posture varies across complaint, settlement and Board decision.

observations.claim: Union-represented workers may request representation in covered investigatory interviews they reasonably believe could lead to discipline.
limits: Current Board-law scope is not generalized to all workers.

observations.claim: The EU Platform Work Directive bars automated processing intended to predict exercise of association, collective bargaining, collective action, information or consultation rights.
limits: Platform-work scope and transposition boundary remain explicit.

observations.claim: The Directive also bars processing of private conversations, including exchanges with other platform workers and their representatives.
limits: This prohibition is not generalized beyond directive scope.

findings.claim: Dissonance cannot be treated as misconduct by default because some critical speech, collective complaint and safety communication sits inside protected-rights frameworks.
limits: No named worker activity is adjudicated by this wave.

findings.claim: A communication-risk model can suppress lawful voice even without an explicit dissent feature if collective complaints, representative contact or negative management sentiment become adverse proxies.
limits: No universal intent or prevalence claim.

findings.claim: Representation changes the adverse-process transaction by preserving collective memory, reducing isolation and contesting management-authored summaries.
limits: Rights differ by jurisdiction, representation status and meeting type.

findings.claim: The protocol should default uncertain speech and collective conduct into a protected-signal hold rather than allowing an automated risk score to become discipline evidence.
limits: Proposed control only; no legal conclusion or adoption.
